newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Aug PPI hit by domestic price increases.
newsitem.headline: S.African Aug PPI hit by domestic price increases.

text.p: A sharp increase in locally produced product prices drove producer inflation to a higher than expected increase in August, according to Central Statistical Service (CSS) data released on Tuesday.

The CSS said producer inflation rose 1.0 percent from July and was up 7.4 percent year-on-year. A Reuters consensus forecast of economists had predicted a 0.9 month-on-month and 7.2 percent year-on-year increase.
The annual rate of increase for locally produced commodities was 8.5 percent after a 1.4 percent month-on-month increase.
Imported inflation, which accounts for about 20 percent of the overall producer price index, remained subdued weighing in with a 0.1 percent month-on-month and 4.5 percent year-on-year contribution.

"The CSS reviewed the price changes contributing to this somewhat surprisingly small monthly increase...and found that the wide-spread increases in the prices of imported manufactured products were offset by decreases in the prices of imported agricultural and mining products," it said.

The service said relatively large monthly increases were recorded in the agricultural products category, where the price index rose 4.8 percent and leather and leather products, which grew 5.9 percent.
Non-metallic products rose 2.3 percent, basic metals grew 1.5 percent, metal products increased 2.9 percent and transport equipment lifted 1.6 percent.
